advancement.kultivator.tempat.tema_pelab: Break a Pirate Raid on a Harbour City.
Win the Fishing Boat Race on Sea Goddess Day.
Collect the keel you ordered from Granny Keel's shipyard.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_pelabuhan_a: A-Lan got her blessing to become a captain after racing %s.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_pelabuhan_b: %s stood guard on the quays when the pirates came for the Lamp Pearl.
A black-sailed junk is raiding the Grand Quay! Black Shark's pirates again!
Pirates looted the warehouses last night. The Overseas Market is shut, and one merchant ship dares not come.
The pirates were driven off the quays last night. The guards drank wine till morning.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_pelabuhan_d: Sea Goddess Day! The Goddess's palanquin comes down to the quay, then there's a fishing boat race in the bay.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_pelabuhan_h: Did you hear? The Black Shark went home to his master, Grandpa Deng, after a duel with %s. They say he will captain a second crossing ship.
The Black Shark knelt at the foot of the lighthouse, and Grandpa Deng hugged him like hauling in a heavy net. The fishers pretended not to cry. %s brought them together.
Captain Black Shark was handed to the Harbourmaster by %s. The Maritime Office will try him.
The Black Shark was led to the Maritime Office with his hands tied by his own mooring rope. He did not resist once. %s walked behind him all the way to the door.
The Black Shark died on the Breakwater by the sword of %s. The sailors are grateful... but some say the sea dislikes blood.
That night Grandpa Deng lit the lamp late. Then he set one little lamp at the end of the Breakwater, facing the sea. Nobody dares ask who it is for, least of all %s.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_pelabuhan_k: A merchant ship from the Western Lands just dropped anchor at the Grand Quay. Its cargo is sold on deck, first come first served.
A merchant ship from another harbour city down the coast just dropped anchor at the Grand Quay. Its cargo is sold on deck, first come first served.
A merchant ship from the Pearl Isles just dropped anchor at the Grand Quay. Its cargo is sold on deck, first come first served.
A merchant ship from the Southern Spice Lands just dropped anchor at the Grand Quay. Its cargo is sold on deck, first come first served.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_pelabuhan_l: The lighthouse is bright again! Granny Keel fitted a new lens brought by %s.
%s won the Fishing Boat Race and took home the Wave Charm!
Granny Keel launched a new ship belonging to %s. Its name is carved on the bow.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_pelabuhan_m: %s uncovered the Shadow Oil smuggling! The Harbourmaster is seizing casks in the Shared Warehouse.
The "lamp oil" casks in the Shared Warehouse turned out to be Shadow Oil. Its smoke is black and smells of rust. %s was the first to smell it.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_pelabuhan_p: The Wind-Guiding Lamp burns blue and gold! %s lit it with Grandpa Deng. The ships are coming home again.
The moment the Lamp was lit, every ship in the bay rang its bell at once. Auntie Yu wept at her stall, and %s stood at the top of the tower beside Grandpa Deng.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_pelabuhan_s: Auntie Yu's Spirit Fish soup is special this year: %s caught the fish.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_pelabuhan_t: Ibrahim's caravan arrived with a parcel for Grandpa Deng. Whatever is inside glows like dawn.
kultivator.cerita.kabar.tema_pelabuhan_u: A-Lan oils her oar with fish oil every morning. She says a slick oar cuts water faster. You can smell it at the temple.
When the sky growls, the boats stay moored. The Sea Goddess does not save those who dare a storm.
When the gulls fly low over the Morning Fish Market, there's wind tomorrow. When they sit still on the warehouse roofs, a storm.
On the twenty-third of each month the Sea Goddess comes down to the quay. Don't fish that morning; join the procession.
The Black Shark was once an ordinary quay boy. They say he knew every reef in the bay blindfolded.
Ibrahim of the Western Lands reads the stars faster than a chart. Even old captains ask him.
The Morning Fish Market opens before the cock crows and shuts before the sun gets hot. Come late, get bones.
The harbour dredge swallows mud day and night. Without it, the Grand Quay channel would silt up in one season.
Ships from the Pearl Isles sometimes carry a Tide Compass. Its needle points to a sea whirlpool, not north.
Captain Gao says in the Boundless Sea there is an island whose market moves with every tide.
Granny Keel curses everyone, but not one of her ships has ever leaked.
Grandpa Deng has kept the light for thirty years. He talks to his lamp like a grandchild.
Zhao Wanli owes half the city, and the other half owes him.
kultivator.cerita.quest.tema_pelabuhan_b: Ibrahim gives you a Small Astrolabe that always points to true north. His book now has a chapter on the eastern sky.
On three different nights, wait at the top of the Guiding Pagoda after dusk until the watch is done.
Ibrahim of the Western Lands is copying the eastern stars into his book and asks for a companion on watch.
kultivator.cerita.quest.tema_pelabuhan_i: The Goddess's soup simmers on the quay, smelling of ginger and sea. Auntie Yu says your name over every bowl.
Catch ten Spirit Fish in the bay (hire a boat at the Fishers' Moorings).
Auntie Yu of the Morning Fish Market needs ten Spirit Fish for the Sea Goddess Day soup.
Bring the ten Spirit Fish to Auntie Yu's stall at the Morning Fish Market.
kultivator.cerita.quest.tema_pelabuhan_l: Wait until your ship is finished on the slipway, then collect its keel at the shipyard.
Your first keel leaves the yard with its name carved on the bow. Granny Keel pretends not to wipe her eyes.
Choose your ship's name with Granny Keel before the keel is collected.
Order a cloud boat or sect ship keel through Granny Keel's shipyard service.
Granny Keel wants to build your first ship at the shipyard, and name it together with you.
kultivator.cerita.quest.tema_pelabuhan_p: Examine the customs records on Lin Haichao's desk: one of the three manifests of the lost ships is forged.
Captain Black Shark waits on the Breakwater. Defeat him, or talk first and challenge him to an honourable Duel of Swords.

The Wind-Guiding Lamp burns blue and gold and its beam reaches the Thousand Reefs again. You are now a Keeper of the Light: the Overseas Market gives you a discount, the crossing ship half fare, and the next Sea Goddess Day is held in your name.
That "lamp oil" is Shadow Oil. Report it to Lin Haichao, or first hear what Zhao Wanli of the Merchants' Council has to say.
A new lens needs Sea-Salt Glass: make it at Granny Keel's kiln, buy it from Ibrahim, or keep Ibrahim company for a night of stargazing. Hand the glass to Granny Keel.
The Lamp Pearl is dead. Take the crossing ship (free this time) to the Boundless Sea, get a Dawn Pearl from an island merchant or a sea serpent, and bring it home to the city.
Hei Sha kneels on the breakwater planks. Decide his fate: hand him to Lin Haichao, reconcile him with his master, or end his sea.
Climb the lighthouse and look at the Wind Lamp's lens up close, then speak with Harbourmaster Lin Haichao at the Maritime Office.
The Wind-Guiding Lamp in the lighthouse is dimming and ships vanish in the fog. Grandpa Deng Ming, the half-deaf lighthouse keeper, asks for help.
The lamp burns bright, and something out at sea is coming for it. Defend the quays tonight.
Ibrahim sent a Dawn Pearl with his caravan. Return to the harbour city.
Bring the Dawn Pearl to Grandpa Deng and relight the Wind-Guiding Lamp.
kultivator.cerita.quest.tema_pelabuhan_t: A-Lan has the Harbourmaster's blessing. Her mooring rope is whole now: one day she will stand on the deck of her own ship.
Beat A-Lan in a boat race in the bay: a practice lap or the Sea Goddess Day Boat Race.
Tell Lin Haichao how A-Lan raced.
A-Lan, the deckhand of the Broken Anchor Tavern, wants to be a captain. The Harbourmaster will only bless her once she has raced a worthy rival in the bay.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_a_lan_l: Is your boat ready? I've been oiling my oar with fish oil for three days.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_a_lan_s: You're sect folk, right? Fast, strong, not afraid of water? I want to be a captain, but the Harbourmaster says my mooring rope is still "frayed": I've never beaten anyone in the bay. Race me! If I lose to someone as good as you and keep my nerve, that's a captain.
Ha! Hire a boat at the Fishers' Moorings, then call me. One lap of the race course. Or beat me in the Boat Race on Sea Goddess Day, if you like a crowd.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_awak.mu: The south-west wind is here, spice-ship season. Want to hear the quay gossip?
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_bea.mul: Seal, pass, scales. Foreign goods pay two in a hundred; smuggled goods are seized and their owner fined.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_bibi_yu: Not ten yet? The bay isn't going anywhere. Go on, go on!
In the bay, of course! Hire a boat at the Fishers' Moorings, two Nilai Batu an hour, then fish with patience. About one catch in ten is a Spirit Fish; its scales glow blue.

Fish! Fresh fish! Eh, you, with the sword, want to help Auntie? On Sea Goddess Day Auntie cooks soup for the whole sailors' quarter, and the Goddess's soup needs Spirit Fish. Ten of them! The fishers are too lazy to go far now.
Ten Spirit Fish. I will find them.
Good child! Bring them to Auntie's stall at the Morning Fish Market. Don't let them cook in the sun!
Oh my, look at those scales! Blue as the Goddess's eyes! Here, here, give them all to me.
You do not carry ten Spirit Fish.
Here's your pay, and the first two bowls of soup, for the angler. If you're in town on Sea Goddess Day, sit on the quay; Auntie will save you another bowl.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_deng_du: He waits on the Breakwater, I saw his sail from the tower. If he has not come, let me flash the lamp twice; that was our sign, long ago.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_deng_mu: Only in the Boundless Sea. Captain Gao Fan sails there every noon; I have spoken to him: for you, this once, free. There is an Isle Market, and its merchants sell a Dawn Pearl to those bold enough to ask (approach them humbly, crouching low). Or take one from a sea serpent's belly. Bring it home, here.

Hei Sha... He was my apprentice once, a skinny boy who knew every reef in this bay by heart. Then the sea called him too loudly. He came for the Lamp Pearl, but its light died long ago. Here, hold it. Feel how cold it is.
Where can a new pearl be found?
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_deng_na: I hear you fought him with honour. Bring him here... no, let me go down. Twenty years I have waited for that boy to come home.
Come, Grandpa. He is on the Breakwater.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_deng_re: The lens is cracked like ice at the start of spring. Once you have seen it, go to the Harbourmaster. That spiral stair has two hundred steps; don't hold the rusty rail.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_deng_sa: The Wind-Guiding Lamp. The city's founders brought a pearl from the Boundless Sea and lit a spirit fire inside it. While it burns, no mortal ship loses its way in the fog. Thirty years I have poured its oil... and only now does it fade.
Eh? Speak up, young one, these old ears belong half to the sea. ...See that lighthouse? My lamp grows dim every night. Its beam once reached the Thousand Reefs; now ships vanish in the fog.
Let me look at the lamp, Grandpa.
Climb to the lamp room at the top of the tower and see the lens with your own eyes. Then find Harbourmaster Lin at the Maritime Office. She has no love for sect folk, but she listens.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_deng_se: Gone into the fog, like the first time he left. But now the lamp is bright. If some night he wishes to come home, this light will find him before the guards do. I will not lock the tower door.

You did what the sea asked, and the captains are safe because of it. I do not blame you. But for twenty years I lit this lamp for a skinny lost boy. Now I light one more little lamp, at the end of the Breakwater, facing the sea. For the boy, not for the captain.
May I help light it?
Until later.
Keeper of the Light! Sit down. Tonight the beam reaches the Thousand Reefs again; the captains bow toward the tower as they pass. Any news from the quays?
How is Hei Sha, Grandpa?
How is Hei Sha, Grandpa?
Do you still think of Hei Sha, Grandpa?
Where did Hei Sha go?
What news have you heard, Grandpa?
Until later.

Every dusk he climbs those two hundred steps with a basket of oil, though I told him my knees are still strong. He captains the second crossing ship, mends the nets of the quay children, and has not lifted a blade once. Yesterday he asked whether the reef at the bay's mouth was still where it used to be. Still there, I said. Same as his home.
Give him my greetings.
Until later.
...Yes. At dusk. Bring a new wick; the old one is eaten by the wind.
I will. He will pretend not to care, then polish that lens twice as long. That is apprentices for you.

Harbourmaster Lin passed a fair sentence: three years pedalling the harbour dredge, clearing mud from the very channels he once plundered. I bring him Auntie Yu's fish soup every twenty-third. He does not speak... but the bowl always comes back empty.
Three years is not long to the sea.
Until later.
True. The sea waits patiently. If he knocks on the tower door in three years, I will open it.
The lamp is bright again! So bright... but brightness invites eyes too. Something out on the sea has been waiting for this light, I can feel it in my knees. Guard the quays tonight.
I will keep watch.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_deng_ti: You took so long that Ibrahim sent this with his caravan: a Dawn Pearl, bought from an island merchant. He says the stars told him to. Keep it safe; Hei Sha will surely know the pearl is in the city.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_deng_up: The Dawn Pearl... its light is like the first morning on the sea, before there were ships, before there were pirates. Come, let us light the Wind Lamp together. The whole quay is waiting.
You do not carry the Dawn Pearl.
Look... the blue, the gold! The ships will come home again, and the next Sea Goddess Day is held in your name. From tonight you are this city's Keeper of the Light, just as I am.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_gao_mut: Grandpa Deng told me, he told me. Free. Hhh... don't tell anyone; if everyone knew, I'd be ruined. We sail at twelve. On land I am afraid of dogs, but at sea, trust me.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_gao_sap: The Black Shark! Captaining a crossing ship! And he sails through fog that sends me home to bed. Hmph. But he brings me tea from the Isle Market, so... I won't bite him. Not yet.
The crossing ship leaves at noon, once a day, except in storms. Except in storms! I am not mad.
I hear there is a second crossing ship.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_gong_le: Ibrahim of the Western Lands has a lump of it, brought from the salt shores across the sea. Pricey, and an odd one: he stares at the stars all night holding a brass disc. Or make it yourself: four handfuls of sand and one Spirit Fish. Hire a boat at the Fishers' Moorings if you have no fish yet.

A new lens? Hah! Common glass cracks in the night chill of the sea, like the one up there now. A lighthouse eye needs Sea-Salt Glass: beach sand, a fish's spirit, white fire and patient hands. Are your hands patient, child?
Teach me to make it at your kiln.
Where else can that glass be had?
Let me see... hm. Clear, no bubbles. Good. I'll fit it myself tonight; old Deng mustn't climb those stairs again. Watch the lighthouse later, child.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_gong_na: Hm! A good name. The sea will remember it. Take your keel when it's done, and don't ram it into the mooring tower!
A ship with no name is like a child with no mother: the sea doesn't know what to call it. Choose, child. I carve the name on its keel before you take it.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_gong_pe: Not ordered yet? Look at the shipyard service, child. I don't build ships out of chatter.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_gong_sa: You stare at my slipway like a child at sweets. Want a ship of your own? A cloud boat from this yard flies straighter than a gull. Order its keel, and then we give it a proper name.
Good! Order through the shipyard service: cloud boat 900, sect ship 4000 Nilai Batu. Then come back to me once the frame stands.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_heisha_: ...That old man? He drove me out when I sank my first ship. "The sea is not yours," he said. And still he poured oil into that lamp, every night, facing the way I sailed? A lie. ...Prove it with a sword, not with words.
An honourable Duel of Swords. If I win, you listen to him.
So you are the one who lit the old lamp again. Do you know how many ships I robbed in the dark? The pearl: hand it over. Or the sea will swallow you the way it swallows everyone who hopes.
Wait. Your master still lights that lamp for you every night.
Hei Sha will not listen to a stranger (needs Good Name 30).
Enough... the sea has decided. My dao lost its heart before its edge. Do what you must.
You will answer to Harbourmaster Lin.
Go home to your master. He waits for you in the tower.
Hei Sha has not yet agreed to hear of his master.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_ibrahim: Look south: seven stars your sailors call "the Goddess's Rudder". In my land they have another name, but they still point home. We meet again at the pagoda after dark.
Until tonight.

Keep me company for one night at the top of the Guiding Pagoda. In my land sailors read the stars the way you read a notice board, but the stars of this eastern sky are still strangers to my book. One night of watching, and the glass is yours.
Very well, tonight.
Perhaps another time.
The stars were on our side that night. Take the glass, and thank you: my book is one page longer now.
Climb to the pagoda top after dusk and wait until the Guiding Star rises above the sea. Then come back to me.
May its light guide the ships home again.
Peace upon you, friend. Sea-Salt Glass? Yes, I brought a lump from the salt shores of the west, for the lens of my spyglass. I could part with it... for 300 Nilai Batu. Or for another price.
I will buy it for 300 Nilai Batu.
You carry less than 300 Nilai Batu.
What is the other price?
Our night of stars is done.
Until later.

Peace upon you. You see this brass disc? An astrolabe, from my land. It reckons the stars so sailors know true north. But under the eastern sky I need three more nights to copy all the Guiding Stars. Will you keep me company?
Three nights at the pagoda. I'm in.
Until later.
The top of the Guiding Pagoda, after dusk, once a night. I bring the tea, you bring the patience.
My star friend! That little astrolabe points to true north, on any sea. And my book now has a chapter on the eastern sky, with your name on the first page.
Thank you, Ibrahim.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_lin_ala: A-Lan says you beat her in the bay, and she smiled as she lost. That is what I was waiting for: a captain who knows how losing feels will not dare a storm out of pride. I give her my blessing. Thank you, sect cultivator.
She will make a fine captain.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_lin_cat: Three manifests from the lost ships, and the quay scale records from the day they sailed. One manifest lies. Match the seals and the weights; remember, our scale weighs the crates too.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_lin_lap: You look like someone who found a rotten fish at the bottom of the basket. Speak.
Those "lamp oil" casks hold Shadow Oil. That is what is choking the lamp.

Shadow Oil... its smoke chokes a spirit flame, and its haze blinds a helmsman. Someone ships it through this city's warehouses. I will seize every cask and find the hand that signed that false seal. But the lens is still cracked. See Granny Keel at the shipyard; if anyone can make glass for the lighthouse's eye, it is her.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_lin_nas: The Black Shark is beaten, the guards say? If you cannot decide, hand him to the harbour's law. We will judge him fairly, more fairly than the sea would.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_lin_red: ...Old Deng. A cracked lens dims the light, yes. But three ships with seasoned masters do not sink because a lamp is a little dim. Something rotten sits in this harbour. If you truly want to help, come back: the customs records of those ships are on my desk.
A sect cultivator in my office. Let me guess: a free crossing, or a little "protection tribute"? Three ships were lost in the fog this month. I have no time for proud swords.
Grandpa Deng sent me. The lighthouse lens is cracked.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_lin_sap: Maritime Office. Customs are a fraction of the cargo, a seal on every crate, and no drawn swords on the quays. Those are my rules.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_lin_sel: I do mind. I wrote three letters of protest to the Council. Then I watched him drag three fishers' nets out of the whirlpool at the Thousand Reefs, in a storm nobody dared sail. I never wrote the fourth letter.
...I did not expect that. This money will buy new mooring ropes for the Fishers' Moorings. I will strike that line in the book. In red ink, so it shows it was struck.

Keeper of the Light. Since the lamp was lit, not one ship has been lost in the fog. I recorded it in the customs book, on the page usually kept for losses. Sit, if you like. But draw nothing in my office.
What was the verdict on Hei Sha?
You don't mind that Hei Sha walks free?

Three years on the dredge. Some say that is too light for a pirate. But he surrendered without blood and showed us himself the warehouses where the oil was hidden. A law that can only hang people will never make the sea any safer.
Fined a thousand Nilai Batu, stripped of his Council seat, and now every seal on the Shared Warehouse has two keys: one in his hand, one in mine. He hates me. That means the rules work.
The casks vanished from the warehouse the night before I came. No papers, no seals, no witnesses. Zhao still smiles in the Council Hall. I can wait. A greedy merchant always writes something down.

I read his ledger when I seized those casks. One line: a hundred and twenty pieces per band, "for the careful guest". I know who that guest was. The lamp burns because of you, so I keep quiet. But I wrote it down too.
I will pay it back into the harbour chest.
You do not carry enough Nilai Batu to repay it.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_lin_ser: The guards stand ready at the Grand Quay and the warehouses. If a black-sailed junk comes, we need every sword, even a proud sect sword.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_mei_sap: Three sticks, for three things: for the ships he sank, for the quay boy he once was, and for your hand that had to decide. The sea accepts them all. The smoke rises straight today; that is a good sign.

Once she was a fisherman's daughter who dreamed of her father and brothers drowning, and flew in her dream to pull them from the waves. Her two guardians stand in the hall: Thousand-Li Eye, who sees every ship, and Wind Ear, who hears every prayer.

The Goddess pulled her father and brothers from the waves without asking whether they had ever sinned. He comes to this temple every morning before he sails, sweeping the incense ash unasked. The Goddess sees him. So do we.

Welcome to the Sea Goddess Temple. Burn a stick of incense for those at sea; the smoke rises and the Goddess watches from afar. On the twenty-third day of each month she comes down to the quay with us.
Tell me about the Sea Goddess.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_seberan: From lands overseas we come, to lands overseas we go. In between, there is a city that buys anything.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_zhao_la: Ah, the careful guest! The whole quay talks of you: a sect cultivator who reads manifests like an old clerk. Sit, the tea is from the Southern Spice Lands.
Those "lamp oil" casks passed through your warehouse, didn't they?

Trade is like the sea, my friend: calm on top, many currents beneath. Those casks... a clerical error. Take these %s as a token of friendship, and let the Harbourmaster busy herself with other matters.
Take the money and keep quiet.
Keep your money. I will report it.
Wise, very wise. The sea loves those who know when to be silent. If the Harbourmaster asks, just say an old lens was bound to crack.
A pity. In a harbour, honest people get wet quickly. Mind the quays at night, guest.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_zhao_sa: Zhao Wanli, head of the Merchants' Council, at your service! Spice, porcelain, glass from overseas... whatever you seek, the Council has a friend who has a friend.
kultivator.cerita.tema_pelabuhan_zhao_se: Honesty is expensive in a harbour. But I hear honest men need not pay night watchmen. Perhaps... I will recount.

Oh. You. The manifest-licker. Because of you I must ask that woman's leave to open my own warehouse. ...But I admit it, guest: since the lamp was lit, the spice ships come twice as often. Profit is still profit.
You can still be honest, Zhao.
My quiet friend! Shh, sit close. The Harbourmaster combs my books like a cat combs a fish basket. You... haven't told her anything, have you? Of course not. We are wise people.
She... knows? And she says nothing? That is more frightening than a fine. That woman keeps debts the way fishers keep salt. I must donate to the temple. A lot.
Shh! Not so loud. They... they asked for the key to the Shared Warehouse tonight. I could not refuse; my debt to the Black Shark is deeper than a trench. Forgive me.
You will answer for this, Zhao.
kultivator.kota_tema.pelabuhan.asal.kota: another harbour city down the coast
kultivator.kota_tema.pelabuhan.bajak.den: Grandpa Deng whispers from the tower: "Hei Sha... is that you, boy?"
kultivator.kota_tema.pelabuhan.bajak.fir: The lights of a black-sailed junk show on the horizon tonight...
kultivator.kota_tema.pelabuhan.bajak.kal: The pirates got away with their loot. The Overseas Market shuts for a day.
kultivator.kota_tema.pelabuhan.bajak.men: Good Name +%1$s · %2$s Nilai Batu from the Town Chest
kultivator.kota_tema.pelabuhan.bajak.sub: Black sails blot out the stars; boarding planks crash onto the Grand Quay.
kultivator.kota_tema.pelabuhan.bintang.m: Ibrahim opens his astrolabe. Be still and watch the Guiding Star...
kultivator.kota_tema.pelabuhan.bintang.s: The night's watch is done (%s). The stars are written in Ibrahim's book.
kultivator.kota_tema.pelabuhan.dewi.sub: The Goddess's palanquin comes down to the quay; drums call the boats.
kultivator.kota_tema.pelabuhan.dokumen.b: Right. The seal and the weight lie: that "lamp oil" is Shadow Oil.
kultivator.kota_tema.pelabuhan.dokumen.c: Seal No. %1$s · %2$s · quay scale %3$s piculs (crates 20 piculs included)
kultivator.kota_tema.pelabuhan.dokumen.d: Lin Haichao sighs and points at the forged manifest: its seal does not match the record.
Not done yet. %s more days on the slipway.
The keel is handed over. Granny Keel slaps the hull once, for luck.
Keel ordered. Watch the slipway: your ship is done in %s days.
That hull style cannot be painted here yet.
Hold your ship's keel in hand to repaint it.
Granny Keel builds this ship only for owners of realm band %s or higher.
Your order is still on the slipway. One ship at a time, says Granny Keel.
There is no order in your name at this shipyard.
kultivator.kota_tema.pelabuhan.habis: That item is sold out for today.
kultivator.kota_tema.pelabuhan.hadiah.gi: Captain Black Shark's dao, forged from wrecked-ship steel.
kultivator.kota_tema.pelabuhan.heisha.me: Hei Sha drops to one knee and drives his dao into the planks: "Enough."
